scenes.text: You’re walking down the street when you suddenly feel a distinct buzz in your pocket, but when you reach down to pull out your phone, there’s absolutely nothing there.
This isn't a random muscle glitch; it's a recognized psychological phenomenon called Phantom Vibration Syndrome, and studies show up to ninety percent of smartphone users experience it regularly.
Your brain has become so accustomed to the constant anticipation of notifications that it now misinterprets simple clothing friction or minor muscle spasms as an incoming call.

This phantom buzz is proof of how deeply modern technology has rewired your physical nervous system, so how often does this happen to you? Let me know in the comments and follow for more fascinating mind facts.
